meta.description: This program displays a paginated list of credit cards to bank staff, filtered by account or showing all cards depending on the user's administrative privileges.
meta.process_description: When a bank staff member accesses the credit card list screen, the program retrieves and displays up to 7 credit cards per page, showing each card's account number, card number, and card status. If the user is an administrator with no specific account context, all credit cards in the system are listed; if the user is a non-admin or an account context has been passed, only cards associated with that specific account are shown. The staff member can navigate through pages of results using function keys (PF7/PF8 for previous/next page) and can select an individual card record to either view its full details (by typing 'S') or update it (by typing 'U'), which transfers control to the card detail or card update program respectively. The program maintains pagination state between interactions by storing the first and last card keys of the currently displayed page in the communication area.

files.CARDDAT: Master credit card file containing all credit card records (card number, account ID, status)
files.CARDAIX: Alternate index path on the card master file allowing retrieval of cards by account ID, used to filter cards for a specific account

business_rules: Administrator users can view all credit cards in the system; non-administrator users can only view cards associated with a specific account passed in the communication area.
A maximum of 7 credit card records can be displayed on a single screen page at one time.
The user may only select one card record at a time for viewing or updating; selecting more than one simultaneously is rejected with an error message.
Valid action codes for a card row are 'S' (view detail) or 'U' (update); any other non-blank entry is rejected as an invalid action code.
Navigation is controlled via function keys: PF7 scrolls back to the previous page, PF8 advances to the next page, PF3 exits the list and returns to the calling program or menu.
Any function key other than Enter, PF3, PF7, or PF8 is treated as invalid and defaulted to Enter behaviour.
If no credit card records are found matching the search or filter criteria, a 'NO RECORDS FOUND' message is displayed to the user.

Pagination state (first card key, last card key, current page number, and whether a next page exists) is preserved in the communication area between screen interactions to support forward and backward navigation.
When entering the program fresh (not returning from a detail or update screen), pagination state is reset to the first page.
Selecting 'S' on a card transfers the user to the card detail view program (COCRDSLC); selecting 'U' transfers the user to the card update program (COCRDUPC), passing the selected card's context.

variables.name: WS-MISC-STORAGE
variables.description: Top-level working storage container grouping all miscellaneous working variables used during credit card list processing, including CICS communication, input validation, selection tracking, and messaging.

variables.name: WS-CICS-PROCESSNG-VARS
variables.description: Group of variables used to capture the outcome of CICS service calls (such as file reads or program transfers) during credit card list operations, enabling the program to detect and handle system-level errors.

variables.name: WS-RESP-CD
variables.description: CICS response code returned after each system call (e.g., reading the card file or transferring to another program). A non-zero value signals that something went wrong during the operation, such as a file not being found or a system error, allowing the program to respond appropriately rather than silently failing.

variables.name: WS-REAS-CD
variables.description: CICS reason code providing additional detail about why a CICS call failed. Used alongside the response code to give bank staff or support teams more specific diagnostic information when a credit card list operation encounters a system error.

variables.name: WS-TRANID
variables.description: The 4-character CICS transaction identifier for the current session. Used to identify which transaction is running the credit card list screen, supporting navigation and program-to-program transfers within the CardDemo application.

variables.name: WS-INPUT-FLAG
variables.description: Overall input validation status flag for the current screen interaction. Indicates whether all user inputs on the credit card list screen (account filter, card filter, action selections) have passed validation checks before the program proceeds.

variables.name: INPUT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that all user inputs on the credit card list screen are valid and the program can safely proceed with the requested action (navigation, selection, or filtering).

variables.name: INPUT-ERROR
variables.description: Condition indicating that one or more user inputs on the credit card list screen failed validation, requiring the program to display an error message and prompt the user to correct their entries before proceeding.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ACCT-FLAG
variables.description: Validation status of the account number filter entered by the user on the credit card list screen. Tracks whether the account number provided to filter the card list is valid, invalid, or was left blank, controlling whether the list is filtered by account or shows all cards.

variables.name: FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the account number entered by the user as a filter is invalid (e.g., non-numeric or does not exist), preventing the card list from being filtered and triggering an error message to the user.

variables.name: FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the account number entered by the user as a filter has passed validation and can be used to retrieve and display only the credit cards associated with that specific account.

variables.name: FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the user left the account number filter field empty. For administrator users, this means all credit cards in the system will be displayed without account-based filtering.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-CARD-FLAG
variables.description: Validation status of the card number filter entered by the user on the credit card list screen. Tracks whether the card number provided to narrow the list is valid, invalid, or was left blank.

variables.name: FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the card number entered by the user as a filter is invalid (e.g., non-numeric or incorrectly formatted), preventing the filtered list from being displayed and triggering an error message.

variables.name: FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the card number entered by the user as a filter has passed validation and can be used to locate and display the specific credit card record matching that number.

variables.name: FLG-CARDFILTER-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the user left the card number filter field empty, meaning no card-level filtering is applied and the list will show all cards matching any other active filter criteria.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-SELECT-COUNTER
variables.description: Running count of how many card rows the user has simultaneously selected on the current page. Used to enforce the business rule that only one card may be selected at a time; if this counter exceeds 1, the program rejects the input and displays an error message.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-SELECT-FLAGS
variables.description: A 7-character string capturing the action codes entered by the user for each of the up to 7 credit card rows displayed on the current page. Each character position corresponds to one displayed card row and holds the action the user wants to perform on that card (view, update, or blank).

variables.name: WS-EDIT-SELECT-ARRAY
variables.description: Array overlay of the 7-character selection flags field, allowing the program to process each card row's action code individually. Enables row-by-row validation of user selections across the displayed credit card list.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-SELECT
variables.description: The action code entered by the user for a single credit card row on the list screen. Valid values are 'S' to view card details or 'U' to update the card; any other non-blank value is treated as an invalid action.

variables.name: SELECT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the user entered a valid action code for a card row — either 'S' to view the card's details or 'U' to update the card. Only these two values are accepted as legitimate selections.

variables.name: VIEW-REQUESTED-ON
variables.description: Condition indicating the user selected 'S' (Select/View) on a specific card row, requesting to navigate to the card detail view screen (COCRDSLC) for that card.

variables.name: UPDATE-REQUESTED-ON
variables.description: Condition indicating the user selected 'U' (Update) on a specific card row, requesting to navigate to the card update screen (COCRDUPC) to modify that card's information.

variables.name: SELECT-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the user left the action code field blank for a particular card row, meaning no action is requested for that card and it should be ignored during processing.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-SELECT-ERROR-FLAGS
variables.description: A 7-character string recording which of the displayed card rows have invalid action codes entered by the user. Each position corresponds to one card row and is used to highlight erroneous selections on the screen so the user knows which entries to correct.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-SELECT-ERROR-FLAGX
variables.description: Array overlay of the selection error flags field, allowing the program to check and set error indicators for each of the 7 card rows individually when validating user action code entries.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-SELECT-ERRORS
variables.description: Individual error indicator for one of the 7 displayed credit card rows. Used to flag rows where the user entered an invalid action code, enabling targeted error highlighting on the list screen.

variables.name: WS-ROW-CRDSELECT-ERROR
variables.description: Error flag for a single credit card row on the list screen. When set to '1', indicates that the action code entered by the user for this specific row is invalid, prompting the screen to highlight the field and display an appropriate error message.

variables.name: WS-ROW-SELECT-ERROR
variables.description: Condition indicating that the user entered an invalid action code (not 'S', 'U', or blank) for this particular card row, triggering an error message and preventing navigation until the user corrects the entry.

variables.name: WS-SUBSCRIPT-VARS
variables.description: Group of loop and index variables used to iterate through the 7 displayed credit card rows during validation and selection processing on the credit card list screen.

variables.name: I
variables.description: General-purpose loop counter used to iterate through each of the up to 7 credit card rows displayed on the current page, for purposes such as validating action codes or populating screen fields.

variables.name: I-SELECTED
variables.description: Index number (1–7) of the specific card row the user has selected for viewing or updating. Identifies which of the displayed credit cards the user wants to act upon, enabling the program to pass the correct card's details to the card detail or update screen.

variables.name: DETAIL-WAS-REQUESTED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the user has selected a valid card row (rows 1 through 7) for viewing or updating. When true, the program knows a specific card has been chosen and can proceed to transfer the user to the appropriate detail or update screen.

variables.name: CICS-OUTPUT-EDIT-VARS
variables.description: Group of working variables used to format and validate data values before displaying them on the credit card list screen, including account ID and CVV code formatting, and screen field protection control.

variables.name: CARD-ACCT-ID-X
variables.description: Account ID associated with a credit card, held as a character string for display formatting purposes on the credit card list screen. Allows the 11-digit account number to be presented to bank staff in a readable format.

variables.name: CARD-ACCT-ID-N
variables.description: Numeric reinterpretation of the account ID field, allowing the program to perform numeric validation or comparison on the account number while sharing the same memory as the display-formatted character version.

variables.name: CARD-CVV-CD-X
variables.description: The 3-digit Card Verification Value (CVV) security code of a credit card, held as a character string for display or validation on the credit card list screen.

variables.name: CARD-CVV-CD-N
variables.description: Numeric reinterpretation of the CVV code field, enabling numeric validation of the security code while sharing storage with the character-formatted CVV display field.

variables.name: FLG-PROTECT-SELECT-ROWS
variables.description: Screen protection control flag that determines whether the action code input fields next to each displayed credit card row are editable or locked. When protected, bank staff cannot enter selections, typically because the user does not have permission to act on the listed cards.

variables.name: FLG-PROTECT-SELECT-ROWS-NO
variables.description: Condition indicating that the action code input fields on the credit card list screen are open for user input, allowing bank staff to enter 'S' or 'U' to select a card for viewing or updating.

variables.name: FLG-PROTECT-SELECT-ROWS-YES
variables.description: Condition indicating that the action code input fields on the credit card list screen are locked and read-only, preventing the user from selecting any card row — typically applied when the user lacks the necessary privileges.

variables.name: WS-LONG-MSG
variables.description: Extended message buffer used to construct detailed diagnostic or informational messages during credit card list processing, such as capturing full error details for logging or debugging purposes when system errors occur.

variables.name: WS-INFO-MSG
variables.description: Short informational message displayed to bank staff on the credit card list screen, providing guidance on available actions (e.g., instructions on how to select a card for viewing or updating).

variables.name: WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE
variables.description: Condition indicating there is no informational message to display to the user on the credit card list screen, meaning the info message area should appear blank.

variables.name: WS-INFORM-REC-ACTIONS
variables.description: Condition indicating the informational message area is set to display instructions to bank staff about how to interact with the credit card list (e.g., 'Enter S to view or U to update a card').

variables.name: WS-ERROR-MSG
variables.description: Error message displayed to bank staff on the credit card list screen when a validation or processing problem occurs, such as an invalid action code, multiple simultaneous selections, or no records found matching the filter criteria.

variables.name: WS-ERROR-MSG-OFF
variables.description: Condition indicating there is no error to report to the user; the error message area on the credit card list screen is blank and no problem has been detected with the current interaction.

variables.name: WS-EXIT-MESSAGE
variables.description: Condition indicating the error message area contains a message informing the user that they are exiting the credit card list screen, displayed when PF3 is pressed to return to the calling program or main menu.

variables.name: WS-NO-RECORDS-FOUND
variables.description: Condition indicating the error message area contains a 'NO RECORDS FOUND' message, displayed when no credit card records match the account or card number filter criteria entered by the user.

variables.name: WS-MORE-THAN-1-ACTION
variables.description: Condition indicating the error message area contains a message telling the user they selected more than one card row simultaneously, which violates the business rule that only one card may be acted upon at a time.

variables.name: WS-INVALID-ACTION-CODE
variables.description: Condition indicating the error message area contains a message informing the user that they entered an unrecognised action code for a card row — only 'S' (view) and 'U' (update) are valid entries.

variables.name: WS-PFK-FLAG
variables.description: Flag indicating whether the function key pressed by the user is a recognised and supported key for the credit card list screen. Helps the program decide whether to process the key's intended action or default to Enter behaviour.

variables.name: PFK-VALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the user pressed a supported function key (Enter, PF3, PF7, or PF8), allowing the program to execute the corresponding navigation or action on the credit card list screen.

variables.name: PFK-INVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the user pressed an unsupported function key on the credit card list screen. The program will treat this as an Enter key press and may display a message informing the user that the key is not valid in this context.

variables.name: WS-CONTEXT-FLAG
variables.description: Flag indicating whether the user is entering the credit card list program for the first time (fresh start) or returning from a card detail or update screen. Controls whether pagination state should be reset to the first page or preserved from the previous interaction.

variables.name: WS-CONTEXT-FRESH-START
variables.description: Condition indicating the user is entering the credit card list screen fresh (not returning from a detail or update screen), causing the program to reset pagination to the first page and clear any previous navigation state.

variables.name: WS-CONTEXT-FRESH-START-NO
variables.description: Condition indicating the user is returning to the credit card list screen from a card detail or update screen, allowing the program to restore the previous pagination state so the user sees the same page they were on before navigating away.

variables.name: WS-FILE-HANDLING-VARS
variables.description: Group of variables used to manage file access operations against the credit card master file (CARDDAT) and its alternate index (CARDAIX), including record identifiers used to position the file cursor for paginated reading.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID
variables.description: Record identifier (key) used to position the credit card file for reading during paginated list display. Composed of the card number and account ID, this key tells the system exactly which card record to start reading from when building the next or previous page of results.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID-CARDNUM
variables.description: The 16-digit credit card number portion of the file record identifier. Used as the primary key component when positioning the credit card master file to retrieve a specific card record or to start reading from a particular point in the paginated list.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID
variables.description: The 11-digit account ID portion of the credit card record identifier used when reading the card file. This is the account number associated with a credit card, used to locate or filter card records belonging to a specific customer account during file I/O operations.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X
variables.description: An alternate character-format view of the account ID field in the card record identifier. Allows the numeric account ID to be treated as raw character data when constructing or comparing file keys during card record retrieval operations.

variables.name: WS-SCRN-COUNTER
variables.description: A counter tracking how many credit card records have been placed onto the current screen page during the page-building process. It increments with each card record added to the display list and is used to enforce the 7-record-per-page business rule.

variables.name: WS-FILTER-RECORD-FLAG
variables.description: A flag that controls whether the credit card record currently being processed should be shown to the user or skipped. Used to enforce access rules — for example, excluding cards that do not belong to the account being viewed by a non-administrator user.

variables.name: WS-EXCLUDE-THIS-RECORD
variables.description: Condition indicating that the current credit card record does NOT meet the filter criteria and should be skipped — it will not be displayed to the bank staff member on the current page.

variables.name: WS-DONOT-EXCLUDE-THIS-RECORD
variables.description: Condition indicating that the current credit card record DOES meet the filter criteria and should be included in the list displayed to the bank staff member on the current page.

variables.name: WS-RECORDS-TO-PROCESS-FLAG
variables.description: A flag controlling the card file reading loop. It signals whether the program should continue reading more card records from the file or stop — used to manage pagination and end-of-file conditions when building each page of results.

variables.name: READ-LOOP-EXIT
variables.description: Condition indicating that the card file reading loop should stop — either because the page is full (7 records reached), no more records exist in the file, or an error has occurred.

variables.name: MORE-RECORDS-TO-READ
variables.description: Condition indicating that the card file reading loop should continue — more card records are available in the file and the current page is not yet full.

variables.name: WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE
variables.description: A structured error message record that is assembled and displayed (or logged) when a file operation against the card master file or its alternate index fails. It captures enough detail for support staff to diagnose the problem.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Fixed label text at the start of the file error message (e.g., 'FILE ERROR: '), providing a human-readable prefix so bank operations staff can immediately identify the message as a file access error.

variables.name: ERROR-OPNAME
variables.description: The name of the file operation that failed (e.g., 'READ', 'STARTBR', 'READNEXT'), helping support staff understand at which step in the card retrieval process the error occurred.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Fixed separator text within the file error message (e.g., ' ON '), used for readability when the error message is displayed to operations staff.

variables.name: ERROR-FILE
variables.description: The name of the file that experienced the error (e.g., 'CARDDAT' or 'CARDAIX'), identifying whether the problem was with the main credit card master file or its account-based alternate index.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Fixed label text within the file error message (e.g., ' RESPONSE CODE: '), providing a readable separator before the CICS response codes for operations staff.

variables.name: ERROR-RESP
variables.description: The primary CICS response code returned when the card file operation failed. This code helps technical support staff identify the category of error (e.g., file not found, end of file, record not found).

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Fixed separator text within the file error message (e.g., ' RESP2: '), providing a readable label before the secondary response code for operations staff.

variables.name: ERROR-RESP2
variables.description: The secondary CICS response code returned when the card file operation failed. Provides additional diagnostic detail beyond the primary response code to help technical staff pinpoint the exact cause of the file access failure.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Trailing padding or punctuation at the end of the file error message, ensuring the message is properly formatted when displayed to operations staff.

variables.name: WS-CONSTANTS
variables.description: A group of fixed constant values used throughout the credit card list program. These define system-wide limits, program names, transaction IDs, map names, and file names that govern how the program navigates between screens and accesses data.

variables.name: WS-MAX-SCREEN-LINES
variables.description: The maximum number of credit card records that can be displayed on a single page of the card list screen (set to 7). This enforces the business rule that no more than 7 cards are shown at one time, requiring the user to page forward or backward to see additional cards.

variables.name: LIT-THISPGM
variables.description: The program name of this credit card list program (COCRDLIC) itself. Used when setting up the communication area to identify the current program to CICS and to other programs in the CardDemo application.

variables.name: LIT-THISTRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID associated with this credit card list program. Used to identify the current transaction when returning control to this screen after navigating to a detail or update program.

variables.name: LIT-THISMAPSET
variables.description: The name of the BMS mapset containing the screen layout for the credit card list display. Used when sending or receiving the card list screen to/from the bank staff member's terminal.

variables.name: LIT-THISMAP
variables.description: The name of the specific BMS map (screen layout) used to display the paginated list of credit cards. Referenced when painting the card list onto the bank staff member's terminal screen.

variables.name: LIT-MENUPGM
variables.description: The program name of the main CardDemo menu. Used when the bank staff member presses PF3 to exit the card list and return to the application's main menu.

variables.name: LIT-MENUTRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID for the main CardDemo menu. Used to transfer control back to the menu transaction when the bank staff member exits the card list screen.

variables.name: LIT-MENUMAPSET
variables.description: The BMS mapset name for the main CardDemo menu screen. Used when navigating back to the menu after the bank staff member exits the card list.

variables.name: LIT-MENUMAP
variables.description: The specific BMS map name for the main CardDemo menu screen. Used to display the correct menu screen when the bank staff member exits the card list.

variables.name: LIT-CARDDTLPGM
variables.description: The program name of the credit card detail view program (COCRDSLC). When a bank staff member selects a card with action code 'S', control is transferred to this program to display the full details of the selected credit card.

variables.name: LIT-CARDDTLTRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID for the credit card detail view program. Used to initiate the card detail transaction when a bank staff member selects 'S' on a card row.

variables.name: LIT-CARDDTLMAPSET
variables.description: The BMS mapset name for the credit card detail screen. Used when transferring to the card detail view program so the correct screen layout is displayed to the bank staff member.

variables.name: LIT-CARDDTLMAP
variables.description: The specific BMS map name for the credit card detail screen. Used to display the card detail view when a bank staff member selects 'S' on a card in the list.

variables.name: LIT-CARDUPDPGM
variables.description: The program name of the credit card update program (COCRDUPC). When a bank staff member selects a card with action code 'U', control is transferred to this program to allow modification of the selected credit card's details.

variables.name: LIT-CARDUPDTRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID for the credit card update program. Used to initiate the card update transaction when a bank staff member selects 'U' on a card row.

variables.name: LIT-CARDUPDMAPSET
variables.description: The BMS mapset name for the credit card update screen. Used when transferring to the card update program so the correct screen layout is presented to the bank staff member.

variables.name: LIT-CARDUPDMAP
variables.description: The specific BMS map name for the credit card update screen. Used to display the card update form when a bank staff member selects 'U' on a card in the list.

variables.name: LIT-CARD-FILE
variables.description: The CICS file name of the credit card master file (CARDDAT). Used in all direct file access operations to read credit card records when browsing the full card list (typically for administrator users).

variables.name: LIT-CARD-FILE-ACCT-PATH
variables.description: The CICS file name of the alternate index path on the card master file (CARDAIX), which allows retrieval of cards by account ID. Used when filtering the card list to show only cards belonging to a specific account — typically for non-administrator users or when an account filter is applied.

variables.name: WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA
variables.description: The program's own communication area that preserves pagination state between screen interactions. This data is passed back and forth between screen displays so the program knows which page of cards is being shown, where to start reading for the next or previous page, and whether more pages exist.

variables.name: WS-CA-LAST-CARDKEY
variables.description: The composite file key (card number + account ID) of the last credit card record displayed on the current page. When the bank staff member pages forward (PF8), this key is used as the starting point to read the next set of card records from the file.

variables.name: WS-CA-LAST-CARD-NUM
variables.description: The 16-digit credit card number of the last card shown on the current page. Combined with the account ID, it forms the file key used to position the file cursor for forward pagination.

variables.name: WS-CA-LAST-CARD-ACCT-ID
variables.description: The 11-digit account ID of the last credit card shown on the current page. Combined with the card number, it completes the file key used to position the file cursor when the bank staff member navigates to the next page.

variables.name: WS-CA-FIRST-CARDKEY
variables.description: The composite file key (card number + account ID) of the first credit card record displayed on the current page. When the bank staff member pages backward (PF7), this key is used to re-read the previous page of card records.

variables.name: WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-NUM
variables.description: The 16-digit credit card number of the first card shown on the current page. Combined with the account ID, it forms the file key used to navigate backward to the previous page of the card list.

variables.name: WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-ACCT-ID
variables.description: The 11-digit account ID of the first credit card shown on the current page. Combined with the card number, it completes the file key used to position the file cursor when the bank staff member navigates to the previous page.

variables.name: WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM
variables.description: The current page number being displayed to the bank staff member in the credit card list. Increments as the user pages forward and decrements as they page backward, giving the user a sense of their position within the full list of cards.

variables.name: CA-FIRST-PAGE
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank staff member is currently viewing the first page of the credit card list. Used to disable the 'previous page' (PF7) navigation option, since there are no earlier records to display.

variables.name: WS-CA-LAST-PAGE-DISPLAYED
variables.description: A flag indicating whether the last available page of credit card results has already been shown to the bank staff member. Used to control whether the 'next page' (PF8) navigation option is available.

variables.name: CA-LAST-PAGE-SHOWN
variables.description: Condition indicating that the last page of credit card records has already been displayed to the bank staff member. When true, the PF8 (next page) key should be disabled or ignored as there are no further records to show.

variables.name: CA-LAST-PAGE-NOT-SHOWN
variables.description: Condition indicating that the last page of credit card records has NOT yet been displayed. When true, the bank staff member may still page forward to see more cards.

variables.name: WS-CA-NEXT-PAGE-IND
variables.description: An indicator flag showing whether additional pages of credit card records exist beyond the current page. Controls whether the PF8 (next page) function key is presented as a valid navigation option to the bank staff member.

variables.name: CA-NEXT-PAGE-NOT-EXISTS
variables.description: Condition indicating that there are no more credit card records beyond the current page. The bank staff member has reached the end of the card list and cannot page forward further.

variables.name: CA-NEXT-PAGE-EXISTS
variables.description: Condition indicating that additional credit card records exist beyond the current page. The bank staff member can press PF8 to advance to the next page of the card list.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-FLAG
variables.description: A flag indicating whether the program is being re-entered after returning from a card detail or card update program. When set, the program restores the previous pagination state rather than resetting to the first page, so the bank staff member returns to the same position in the card list.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-FLAG-OFF
variables.description: Condition indicating that the program is being entered fresh (not returning from a detail or update screen). Pagination state will be reset to the first page of the card list.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-FLAG-ON
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank staff member has returned to the card list after viewing or updating a card. The program will restore the previously displayed page rather than starting from the beginning of the list.

variables.name: WS-SCREEN-DATA
variables.description: A group area holding the data for all card rows currently displayed on the screen. Contains the card information (card numbers, account IDs, statuses) for up to 7 credit card records shown to the bank staff member on the current page.

variables.name: WS-ALL-ROWS
variables.description: A single contiguous character field representing all 7 rows of credit card data on the current screen page combined. Allows the entire screen's card data to be treated as one block — useful for clearing or copying all displayed card rows at once.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A structured redefinition of the combined screen row data, allowing each of the 7 individual credit card rows to be accessed separately by their component fields (card number, account ID, status) while sharing the same memory as the WS-ALL-ROWS block.

variables.name: WS-SCREEN-ROWS
variables.description: Represents one of up to 7 credit card record rows displayed on a single page of the card list screen. Each occurrence holds the data for one credit card entry shown to the bank staff member, supporting the business rule that a maximum of 7 cards can be displayed per page.

variables.name: WS-EACH-ROW
variables.description: Groups all the data fields belonging to a single displayed row on the credit card list screen, representing one complete credit card entry as seen by the bank staff member.

variables.name: WS-EACH-CARD
variables.description: Groups the specific credit card attributes (account number, card number, and card status) that are displayed for a single card record in the list, representing the key identifying and status information a bank staff member needs to identify and act on a card.

variables.name: WS-ROW-ACCTNO
variables.description: The account number associated with a credit card displayed in a row on the list screen. This allows bank staff to identify which customer account the card belongs to, and is also used as a filter criterion to restrict the card list to cards belonging to a specific account for non-administrator users.

variables.name: WS-ROW-CARD-NUM
variables.description: The 16-digit credit card number displayed in a row on the card list screen. This is the primary identifier of the credit card that bank staff use to distinguish individual cards, and it forms part of the card key used for pagination and for passing context when navigating to the card detail or update programs.

variables.name: WS-ROW-CARD-STATUS
variables.description: The current status of a credit card displayed in a row on the list screen (e.g., active, inactive, blocked). This gives bank staff an immediate at-a-glance view of whether a card is usable, helping them quickly assess the card's standing without needing to navigate to the full card detail screen.

variables.name: WS-COMMAREA
variables.description: The working storage copy of the communication area used to pass data between this credit card list program and other programs in the CardDemo application (such as the card detail program COCRDSLC or the card update program COCRDUPC). It carries session context including user identity, administrative privileges, selected card and account information, and pagination state (first/last card keys, current page number) so that navigation and program transfers work correctly.

variables.name: DFHCOMMAREA
variables.description: The CICS-provided communication area received by this program when it is invoked. It contains the data passed from the previously executing program (such as the menu or a card detail/update program), including user session information, pagination state, and context needed to determine whether the program is being entered fresh or re-entered after returning from a sub-program.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: An unused placeholder byte at the start of the CICS communication area (DFHCOMMAREA). It has no direct business meaning but is used for technical alignment or compatibility purposes, ensuring the subsequent data fields in the communication area are correctly positioned when the program is called by CICS.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN
paragraphs.description: This is the main orchestration paragraph that controls the entire credit card list screen workflow: it initialises the session, interprets the staff member's key press, and routes the interaction to the correct business action — whether that is displaying a page of cards, navigating between pages, viewing card details, updating a card, or returning to the main menu.

paragraphs.name: COMMON-RETURN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph finalises the current screen interaction and hands control back to the CICS transaction manager, preserving the program's identity and full session state so the next user action can be correctly routed and the pagination context is not lost between screen interactions.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point of the main processing routine for the credit card list program. It marks the end of the program's primary business logic flow, allowing control to return cleanly to the calling environment after all screen interactions, pagination, and card selection processing have been completed.

paragraphs.name: 1000-SEND-MAP
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the complete preparation and delivery of the credit card list screen to the bank staff member, coordinating all steps from screen initialisation through to final display. It sequences six distinct preparation stages to ensure the screen is fully built, validated, and rendered with the correct card records, navigation state, and user messages before being presented.

paragraphs.name: 1000-SEND-MAP-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the screen-sending routine, marking the end of the process that presents the credit card list to the bank staff member. It acts as a structural boundary ensuring control returns cleanly to the calling logic after the screen has been dispatched.

paragraphs.name: 1100-SCREEN-INIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph initialises the credit card list screen by clearing any previous display data and populating the screen header with standard identifying information (titles, transaction name, program name, current date, time, and page number), ensuring the screen is ready for a fresh rendering before card records are loaded.

paragraphs.name: 1100-SCREEN-INIT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the screen initialisation routine, marking the end of the process that prepares the credit card list screen for display. It contains no business logic itself, acting purely as a structural boundary that signals completion of the initialisation phase.

paragraphs.name: 1200-SCREEN-ARRAY-INIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph populates the credit card list screen with up to 7 card records retrieved from the system, transferring each card's account number, card number, and status into the corresponding display row. Only rows that contain actual card data are populated; empty slots (where no card was retrieved) are left blank on screen.

paragraphs.name: 1200-SCREEN-ARRAY-INIT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the screen display initialisation routine, marking the end of the process that prepares the credit card list rows for presentation to the bank staff member.

paragraphs.name: 1250-SETUP-ARRAY-ATTRIBS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph configures the interactive state of each of the 7 card selection input fields on the credit card list screen, making each field either protected (read-only) or open for staff input, and highlighting any row where the staff member entered an invalid action code by turning it red and flagging it with an error marker.

paragraphs.name: 1250-SETUP-ARRAY-ATTRIBS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the screen field attribute setup routine, marking the end of the process that configures which card list rows are editable or protected on the display screen.

paragraphs.name: 1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph prepares the credit card list screen for display by populating the account and card number filter fields with the appropriate values and applying visual indicators (colour highlighting and cursor positioning) to guide the staff member's attention to any invalid input fields.

paragraphs.name: 1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the screen attribute setup routine, marking the end of the process that configures display properties (such as field protection and input availability) for the credit card list screen. It contains no business logic itself, acting purely as a structural terminator for the paragraph.

paragraphs.name: 1400-SETUP-MESSAGE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph determines and sets the appropriate user-facing message to display at the bottom of the credit card list screen, based on the current navigation context and page state. It informs staff whether they have reached the boundary of available pages, or guides them on available actions for the displayed card records.

paragraphs.name: 1400-SETUP-MESSAGE-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a structural exit point for the message setup routine, acting as a no-operation placeholder that allows the program to cleanly conclude the message preparation phase before returning control to the calling logic.

paragraphs.name: 1500-SEND-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph renders the credit card list screen to the bank staff member's terminal, displaying the current page of card records and making the screen ready for user input. It clears any previous screen content and positions the cursor so the staff member can immediately interact with the displayed results.

paragraphs.name: 1500-SEND-SCREEN-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the screen-sending routine, marking the end of the process that presents the credit card list to the bank staff member. It acts as a structural boundary in the program flow, ensuring control returns cleanly to the calling logic after the screen has been dispatched.

paragraphs.name: 2000-RECEIVE-MAP
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the capture and validation of staff input from the credit card list screen. It first collects what the user has entered or selected, then applies business rules to verify that the input is acceptable before any further processing occurs.

paragraphs.name: 2000-RECEIVE-MAP-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This is a structural exit point that marks the end of the screen input reception routine. It serves as a no-operation boundary paragraph, allowing the program to cleanly return control after processing the staff member's screen entries and function key selections.

paragraphs.name: 2100-RECEIVE-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph captures the bank staff member's input from the credit card list screen, reading any account/card filter criteria entered and the action codes (S/U) the user typed against each of the up to 7 displayed card rows. It transfers all submitted screen data into the program's working storage so it can be validated and acted upon.

paragraphs.name: 2100-RECEIVE-SCREEN-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a structural exit point for the screen input processing routine. It marks the end of the section that handles receiving and interpreting staff input from the credit card list screen, allowing control to return to the calling logic.

paragraphs.name: 2200-EDIT-INPUTS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the full validation of all user inputs on the credit card list screen before any navigation or selection action is processed. It sequentially validates the account filter, the card filter, and any row-level selection actions entered by the staff member.

paragraphs.name: 2200-EDIT-INPUTS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the input validation routine, marking the end of all credit card list filtering and user-input checks. It provides a structured return path once all account number, card number, and action code validations have been completed.

paragraphs.name: 2210-EDIT-ACCOUNT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates the account number filter entered by the bank staff member before the credit card list is retrieved. It ensures the account number is either intentionally left blank (to show all cards) or is a valid 11-digit numeric value suitable for filtering the card list.

paragraphs.name: 2210-EDIT-ACCOUNT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the account number validation routine, allowing the program to cleanly return control to whichever part of the credit card listing process invoked the account validation check.

paragraphs.name: 2220-EDIT-CARD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates the card number filter entered by the bank staff member on the credit card list screen. It determines whether the card number is absent, non-numeric, or valid, setting the appropriate filter state and error messaging to control how the card list will be retrieved and displayed.

paragraphs.name: 2220-EDIT-CARD-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the card input validation routine, marking the end of the card number editing and validation process before control returns to the calling logic.

paragraphs.name: 2250-EDIT-ARRAY
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates the action codes entered by bank staff against the displayed list of credit cards, enforcing the business rule that only one card may be selected at a time and that only recognised action codes ('S' to view or 'U' to update) are permitted.

paragraphs.name: 2250-EDIT-ARRAY-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the card selection validation routine. It marks the end of the process that checks whether the staff member's row selections are valid (single selection, valid action code), allowing control to return to the calling logic.

paragraphs.name: 9000-READ-FORWARD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves the next page of credit card records from the master file, applying account-level filters where applicable, and populates up to 7 rows on the screen while recording pagination state (first and last card on the page) so the user can navigate forward and backward through the full list.

paragraphs.name: 9000-READ-FORWARD-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the forward page navigation routine, marking the end of the process that reads the next page of credit card records. It acts as a structural boundary in the program, allowing the forward-read logic to cleanly conclude before control returns to the main processing flow.

paragraphs.name: 9100-READ-BACKWARDS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves the previous page of credit card records by reading backwards through the card master file, starting from the first card shown on the current page. It populates up to 7 screen rows with card details (card number, account ID, and active/inactive status) in reverse order to present the correct prior page to the bank staff member.

paragraphs.name: 9100-READ-BACKWARDS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph closes the backward browsing session on the credit card master file after the program has finished reading records in reverse order for previous-page navigation. It is a clean-up exit point that releases the file browsing resources once backward pagination is complete.

paragraphs.name: 9500-FILTER-RECORDS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph determines whether a retrieved credit card record should be included in or excluded from the current page of results, by checking whether the card's account ID and card number match any active filter criteria entered by the user. It acts as a gatekeeper, ensuring only relevant cards are displayed based on the staff member's search context.

paragraphs.name: 9500-FILTER-RECORDS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the exit point for the card record filtering routine, marking the end of the logic that determines whether a retrieved credit card should be included in or excluded from the displayed list. It is a structural boundary paragraph with no additional business logic of its own.

paragraphs.name: SEND-PLAIN-TEXT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles a critical error condition by displaying a plain error message to the bank staff member's screen and immediately terminating the program session. It is used as a last-resort communication mechanism when the normal screen layout cannot be rendered.

paragraphs.name: SEND-PLAIN-TEXT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a simple exit point after sending plain text output to the screen, primarily intended for debugging purposes during development and should not be triggered in normal bank staff operations.

paragraphs.name: SEND-LONG-TEXT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles the display of a full-screen plain-text message to the bank staff member, typically used to communicate a critical error or system-level notification that requires the entire screen. After sending the message, the program terminates its current transaction cycle and returns control to CICS, ending the interaction.

paragraphs.name: SEND-LONG-TEXT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the long-text sending routine, providing a clean termination marker that allows other parts of the program to transfer control here when the screen-sending process is complete.
